clue.text: Alluring tart out on the job

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the four letters of the word tart are rearranged

parts.note: someone on the job is working, busy, active

explanation.surface: A streetwalker plying her trade looks enticing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' tempts as the definition or a pastry; it is anagram fodder, with 'out' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something appealing that draws people towards it.

clue.text: Learner inside, making for lecture

indicators.note: the learner's letter goes inside the phrase for making for

parts.note: taking to can mean heading for, as in taking to the hills
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A trainee is indoors, heading off to a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lecture' is a noun here: a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding or telling-off is a lecture in the sense of a reprimand.

clue.text: Animal like badger left set with some speed

parts.note: a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: A creature resembling a badger moved off at a fair pace.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger of Africa and Asia goes by this name.

clue.text: Seal's cry or squeak

parts.note: to seal is to close
a call is a cry

explanation.surface: A seal makes a bark or a squeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow squeak is a near miss, an escape by a whisker.

clue.text: God has no time for evil

indicators.note: the word for a god lacks the letter for time, so it is taken out

parts.note: an immortal is a god

explanation.surface: A deity is too busy to bother with wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct that is wicked or morally wrong.

clue.text: Words unsaid may be

parts.note: words taken back are said to be swallowed, as in having to take back a boast

explanation.surface: Things left unspoken may go unsaid.
explanation.walkthrough: To eat your words is to retract what you said, so unsaid words have been swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retracted words are said to have been swallowed, from the idiom about taking back a claim.

clue.text: Violently throw dart

definitions.meaning: to hurl something down hard, smashing it
to rush or move off quickly

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers hurling something down hard and making a sudden quick run.

clue.text: Perhaps each and every one without a partner is taken here

definitions.text: Perhaps each and every one without a partner is taken here

parts.words: Perhaps each and every one without a partner is taken here
parts.note: a venue where single people are asked onto the floor; the clue words also hint at the letters of each and plus all

explanation.surface: Anyone unattached gets claimed at this venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A public room for ballroom dancing, where people without partners are asked to take the floor.

clue.text: Creator of American cabin and English mansion

definitions.meaning: Harriet Beecher ... wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin
... House in Buckinghamshire, now a school

explanation.definitionFit: The author of Uncle Tom's Cabin shares a name with a great Buckinghamshire country house.

clue.text: Declared party policy — stay with this ticket

definitions.meaning: the manifesto a political party stands on
a railway ticket lets a non-traveller stay at the station's waiting area beside the track

explanation.definitionFit: A party's manifesto and the raised area beside railway tracks share a name; British stations once sold tickets just to go there.

clue.text: Cheap containers

definitions.meaning: two vessels, a can and a pot, side by side

explanation.definitionFit: A shoddy, second-rate thing is called by a word that splits into two vessels, a can and a pot.

clue.text: Fish part that is shown in Angler's Guide

parts.note: the breathing organ of a fish
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An instruction manual for fishermen shows a fish's anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' looks like a book but is a person: a Scottish attendant who guides anglers or hunters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghillie is a Scottish attendant who helps a sportsman find fish or game.

clue.text: Getting plastered? Stop before getting thrown into the street

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the abbreviation for street, as if tossed into it

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a street
a stop is an end
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone drunk is told to stop before being thrown out onto the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests drunk but here means coated with plaster; a rendered wall has had its plaster coat put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a wall is to coat it with plaster, so a rendered wall has been given that coat.

clue.text: Wise man — beginning at back of Times

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a wise man is shifted to the end

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A learned man starts reading from the back page of the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the definition: long periods, eras.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras or long periods are both called this, as in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Heat burns distressed one, perhaps

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters of heat burns are scrambled

explanation.surface: Hot sun scorches a suffering beachgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges HEAT BURNS; the whole clue also describes someone lying in the sun getting scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lying out in the sun is just the sort whom heat burns.

clue.text: Fidelity, say, during marriage

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say goes inside the word for marriage, so it comes during it

parts.note: a marriage is an alliance between families
e.g., for example, is a way of saying say

explanation.surface: Faithfulness is expected, so they claim, in a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty, especially to a sovereign or cause, is faithfulness.

clue.text: Unusual old earring with no centre? Not this one!

definitions.text: Unusual old earring with no centre? Not this one!

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters put into an odd new order
the middle letter of the word earring is dropped

explanation.surface: An odd antique earring lacks a middle stone; this kind would have one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no centre' drops the middle R of EARRING; 'Unusual' rearranges OLD + EARING. This ornate earring has a large central stone, hence 'Not this one!'
explanation.definitionFit: A girandole is an ornate earring or pendant with a central stone ringed by smaller ones.

clue.text: State making provision

definitions.meaning: a state or situation, as in good shape
a proviso or stipulation in a contract

explanation.definitionFit: The same word serves for a state of being and a stipulation in an agreement.

clue.text: Bluebottle making you run into place with no escape

indicators.note: the word for run goes inside the word for a trapping place

parts.note: a corner is a position one cannot get out of
to flow is to run, as liquid does

explanation.surface: A housefly drives you into a spot you cannot escape from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottle' is not the fly but the blue flower of cornfields, which has that old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is an old country name for the blue-flowered cornfield plant.

clue.text: Starts buffeting through rough sea and wind

indicators.note: rough implies churned up, so the letters of sea and wind are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough sea and gale start pounding a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges SEA WIND; 'through' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To wade in is to launch an attack vigorously, piling into someone.

clue.text: Light soil

definitions.meaning: to light is to alight, come down and settle

explanation.definitionFit: Coming down to rest and the earth itself share one word.

clue.text: Bolted seconds — stuffed

parts.note: crammed means packed full

explanation.surface: Someone wolfed down second helpings, eating till full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted' suggests gobbling food, which the surface plays on; here it means ran off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean fled or ran off in a hurry.

clue.text: Mark showing omission of name from permit, say

indicators.note: the letter for name is taken away from the permit word

parts.note: a carnet is a customs permit, one example of a permit

explanation.surface: A stamp on a licence shows a name left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A carnet is a customs document letting goods or a vehicle cross borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark shaped like a small inverted V shows where something must be inserted.

clue.text: Short working days for a period of weeks

parts.note: Mon and Th are the short forms of Monday and Thursday, two working days
Th is the abbreviation for Thursday

explanation.surface: A reduced working week lasts several weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar unit of about four weeks.

clue.text: With arrival of starter, one may soon be on a lap

definitions.text: With arrival of starter, one may soon be on a lap

parts.words: With arrival of starter, one may soon be on a lap
parts.note: reads like a race beginning with the starter's gun, but describes the cloth a diner spreads on their knees when the first course comes

explanation.surface: Once the starter fires, a runner will soon be on the first circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner spreads this cloth on their knees when the first course of a meal arrives.

clue.text: Push, say, to make bike move

indicators.note: say tells us the word for push is spoken and the sound gives a different spelling

parts.note: to push drugs is to peddle them

explanation.surface: Give it a shove to get the bicycle going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push' looks like a shove, but it means sell, as a drug pusher does.
explanation.definitionFit: To work a bicycle's foot levers is how a rider propels it.

clue.text: Old city church, home to ragged rascal

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
in means at home

explanation.surface: An ancient city's church shelters a scruffy rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is a scruffy, mischievous child.

clue.text: Such feet will be seen below a pair of longs

definitions.text: Such feet will be seen below a pair of longs

parts.words: Such feet will be seen below a pair of longs
parts.note: seems to picture feet under long legs, but describes poetic feet marked by two long syllables

explanation.surface: Feet appear at the bottom of a pair of long legs.
explanation.walkthrough: In verse, a foot is a unit of syllables; the spondee is the foot of two long syllables, marked by two long symbols above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spondee is a metrical foot of two long syllables, and this adjective describes such feet.

clue.text: What's needed for porridge?

parts.note: oatmeal must be kept moving with a spoon as it cooks, and in British slang porridge is a prison sentence, served in jail

explanation.surface: A cook asks what to do to make oatmeal.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang: doing porridge means serving a prison sentence, and stir is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge must be mixed with a spoon as it cooks, and the same word is slang for the jail where porridge is served.

clue.text: Deer bearing unusual antler found in remote area

indicators.note: the deer word carries the other letters inside it, as if bearing them

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of antler set out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A deer with oddly shaped antlers turns up in the backwoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link: the definition is 'remote area', the back country far from the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The back country lying well away from coasts and towns is a remote region.
